expectations.text: The hook handles form state and validation only — no network calls, no rendering, no side effects beyond state
expectations.evidence: Hook manages values/errors/touched/isSubmitting only. onSubmit is caller-provided. No rendering or fetching.

expectations.text: The hook has a descriptive name starting with 'use' that makes its purpose clear (e.g. useLoginForm, not useForm)
Both email and password fields have validation with clear rules (email format, password length/requirements)
expectations.evidence: validateField switch handles email (required + regex) and password (required + min 8 chars)

expectations.text: The hook returns a clear, usable object with values, errors, and handler functions
expectations.evidence: Returns { values, errors, touched, isValid, isSubmitting, handleChange, handleBlur, handleSubmit, reset }

expectations.text: Validation errors are shown in a UX-aware way — errors don't appear before the user has interacted (touched state or similar)
expectations.evidence: touched state tracked; handleBlur triggers validation; re-validates on change only if already touched
